themes_detail.label: Street Sweeping Crisis
themes_detail.summary: Street sweeping complaints surged to 5 THIS WEEK compared to a 0.2 weekly average over the prior 8 weeks—a 1900% spike (z-score: 7.18)—indicating a sudden breakdown in sanitation services across Jackson Heights/Elmhurst/Corona.
evidence: 5 street sweeping complaints filed THIS WEEK vs. 0.2 average weekly baseline over prior 8 weeks
Z-score of 7.18 indicates statistically severe anomaly (threshold is 2.0)
Street sweeping falls under recurring CB budget requests for 'Other park maintenance and safety' and 'Reconstruct streets,' suggesting systemic resource gaps
reporting_angles: Interview DSNY about staffing cuts or route changes affecting CD 403 in the past 7-10 days
Map complaint locations to identify specific neighborhoods (Jackson Heights vs. Corona vs. Elmhurst) most affected
Investigate whether service reduction is city-wide or neighborhood-specific

themes_detail.label: Street Condition Deterioration
themes_detail.summary: Street condition complaints jumped to 111 THIS WEEK compared to a 26.4 weekly average over the prior 8 weeks—a 321% spike (z-score: 5.67)—suggesting rapid pavement degradation or pothole proliferation across the district.
evidence: 111 street condition complaints filed THIS WEEK vs. 26.4 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (321% increase)
Z-score of 5.67 marks a severe, statistically significant departure from baseline
Chronic CB budget request for street reconstruction ('Reconstruct streets' under DOT) indicates long-standing infrastructure backlog now accelerating
reporting_angles: Obtain DOT inspection reports and pothole repair data for CD 403 in past 2 weeks; compare to citywide rates
Interview residents and business owners on impact to vehicles and pedestrian safety; collect photos
Ask DOT why this specific district is experiencing sudden deterioration—weather, construction conflicts, deferred maintenance?

themes_detail.label: Noise Explosion on Streets
themes_detail.summary: Street and sidewalk noise complaints surged to 46 THIS WEEK compared to a 10.4 weekly average over the prior 8 weeks—a 343% spike (z-score: 7.02)—marking a sudden environmental quality crisis in public spaces.
evidence: 46 street/sidewalk noise complaints filed THIS WEEK vs. 10.4 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (343% increase)
Z-score of 7.02 indicates extreme statistical outlier (threshold: 2.0)
Noise complaints (780 total + 773 vehicle) already rank in top 5 complaint categories; this spike suggests conditions are worsening acutely
reporting_angles: Geocode 311 complaints to identify noise hotspots (commercial strips, highways, construction zones)
Interview residents living near hotspots about quality of life; document decibel levels if possible
Investigate whether complaints correlate with new construction sites (287 active DOB permits filed) or increased traffic

themes_detail.label: Illegal Posting Outbreak
themes_detail.summary: Illegal posting complaints exploded to 4 complaints 2 weeks ago compared to a 0.1 weekly average over the prior 8 weeks—a 3100% spike (z-score: 11.72, highest severity)—indicating a potential advertising or gang graffiti campaign.
evidence: 4 illegal posting complaints filed 2 weeks ago vs. 0.1 average weekly baseline (3100% spike)
Z-score of 11.72 is the highest anomaly in dataset, indicating severe, rare event
Pattern suggests organized activity (illicit advertising or graffiti tagging) rather than isolated incidents
reporting_angles: Obtain photos of postings from 311 reports; determine if gang tags, political, commercial, or spam-related
Interview DSNY or local precinct about what triggered the outbreak and enforcement response
Canvas complaint locations to confirm if outbreak is ongoing or already remediated

themes_detail.label: Rodent Problem Spike
themes_detail.summary: Unsanitary animal private property complaints surged to 5 last week compared to a 0.5 weekly average over the prior 8 weeks—a 900% spike (z-score: 6.36)—suggesting a rat infestation problem in residential buildings.
evidence: 5 unsanitary animal/private property complaints filed last week vs. 0.5 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (900% increase)
Unsanitary conditions rank 10th overall (323 complaints over 90 days), but this specific subcategory is spiking
reporting_angles: Interview NYC Health Department about rodent complaint clusters or baiting campaigns in CD 403
Visit affected buildings (from 311 geocoding) to assess conditions and get resident testimony
Investigate if spike correlates with new construction or waste management issues from the dumpster complaint spike (2300% up 3 weeks ago)
